body: Crude oil climbed above $99 a barrel on Thursday, its highest level in more than a month, as escalating tensions in the Middle East and reports of planned US strikes on Iran rattled markets. According to reports, US and Israeli military officials have drawn up plans for renewed attacks after next month's midterm elections, with Iran's energy infrastructure expected to be a primary target. The US has also ordered non-emergency government personnel and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, following an uptick in attacks by Iran-aligned Houthi forces. The directive was issued after an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, on Saudi Arabia's east coast, on Wednesday. In a further sign of heightened security concerns, Saudi Aramco has reportedly told employees to evacuate its headquarters in Dhahran and work remotely. Aramco facilities have been repeatedly targeted by Houthi attacks in recent years. Together, these developments have intensified fears of prolonged disruptions to oil supplies from the region. title: Argentina's Retail Sales Surge in August
body: Argentina's retail sales rose 24.3% year-on-year to ARS 698.56 billion in August 2026, accelerating from a 23% increase in July. Among the main categories, entertainment and leisure posted the strongest expansion, up 62.8%, followed by furniture, home décor and textiles (41.6%), sporting goods and accessories (36.4%), and perfumery and pharmacy (33%). Sales at food courts, food outlets and kiosks advanced 28.1%, while bookstore and stationery sales and other categories each grew 26.1%. Clothing, footwear and leather goods increased 17%, and toy sales were up 13.5%. Electronics, household appliances and computing was the only segment to contract, slipping 4%. Regionally, retail sales climbed 31.6% in the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires and 20.4% across the 24 districts of Greater Buenos Aires. In the rest of the country, sales rose 20.1% in the Pampas region and 23.9% in Cuyo, while the Northern and Patagonia regions recorded increases of 21.9% and 32.2%, respectively. title: Rosneft stretches refinery repairs from days to months as Ukraine strikes bite
body: The main effect is on refined products rather than crude. Slower repairs mean Russian refining capacity stays offline for longer, keeping diesel and gasoil exports constrained just as the Northern Hemisphere heating season begins and middle distillate markets are already tight. That supports diesel crack spreads and refining margins elsewhere. When Russian refinery runs fall, more crude is typically freed up for export, which can partly offset the supply impact on crude markets. Even so, Brent near $113 is being driven far more by the risk of renewed US strikes on Iran than by Russia. For US consumers, the news makes a quick fall in diesel prices, now around $6.30 a gallon, even less likely before the midterm elections. --- Earlier: Trump invokes Defense Production Act for oil as pump prices bite 12 days before midterms --- Rosneft has concluded that rebuilding refineries only to see them hit again is a losing game, which suggests Russia's fuel export capacity may stay impaired for months, not weeks. Summary: Rosneft is deliberately slowing refinery repairs at most of its plants, stretching work that could take days into months, Bloomberg reported. Refineries brought back online within weeks of attacks were struck again as repairs neared completion. Rosneft officials have privately warned that the costs cannot be sustained, and that a few more months of war could cause severe, lasting damage to the business.

title: Western Digital CEO says AI data beats compute as long-term bet after 55% revenue jump
body: The after-hours drop despite a clear beat suggests positioning, not fundamentals, is driving the moment. The growing share of orders from neoclouds is a double-edged sword: it widens the customer base but links Western Digital more closely to a group facing funding strain, so credit stress among AI infrastructure providers is now a risk to watch for storage names. Thursday's chip rout shows how quickly sentiment toward the whole AI supply chain can change, regardless of company results. --- Earlier: SK hynix drops US IPO plan for Solidigm, once eyed at up to $150 billion valuation --- Western Digital is selling more storage at much higher prices and argues data will outlast compute as the AI opportunity, but investors locked in gains instead of buying the pitch. title: SK hynix drops US IPO plan for Solidigm, once eyed at up to $150 billion valuation
body: For SK Hynix shareholders, the decision removes an overhang. Investors had worried that a separate US listing would dilute the parent's economic interest and add to the holding-company discount across a group that already includes several listed entities. That could offer some support to the shares, which have dropped about 30% since late September to near six-month lows. The move also signals that the window for large AI hardware listings has narrowed after this month's chip sell-off and the turmoil around neocloud funding. Next week's third-quarter results will now take focus, along with whatever funding route SK hynix chooses for Solidigm's expansion. ---- SK Hynix has pulled the plug on Solidigm's US float as falling chip valuations make the timing unattractive, easing a dilution worry for its own shareholders but leaving the unit's funding question open. Summary: SK Hynix has decided not to pursue a US initial public offering of Solidigm, its US-based NAND flash and solid-state drive subsidiary. The company said it ended the IPO review because of market conditions and share price trends. It said Solidigm still needs investment to grow and that it will keep looking at other ways to enhance shareholder value. Reports in recent weeks suggested a listing as early as 2027 that could value Solidigm at up to $150 billion and raise $10 billion to $15 billion, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley reportedly picked as lead banks.

title: ECB preview: MUFG sees October hold, two hikes ahead. See EUR/USD year end at 1.12
body: The French-German 10-year spread is the key gauge: MUFG's scenarios put it at about 170 basis points in its base case and above 200 in a crisis, levels last associated with the euro zone debt crisis. title: Australia flash PMI: private sector shrinks for first time in five months as prices rise
body: The survey shows weaker activity alongside firmer inflation, a difficult mix for rate expectations. Falling output argues against further tightening, while faster input and output price growth argues against easing. That uncertainty could add volatility to Australian dollar and short-dated bond pricing as traders weigh the two signals. Energy is a key channel: firms cited higher energy, shipping and commodity costs, so sustained oil prices above $110 a barrel are likely to keep feeding through to Australian business costs and consumer prices. Falling business confidence also points to a risk of softer investment and hiring intentions into year-end, which equity investors in domestically focused sectors are likely to watch. --- Earlier, looks like more rate pain ahead: RBA's Hauser puts November hike in play --- Australia's private sector slipped into contraction in October as higher prices and borrowing costs hit demand, yet cost pressures intensified, leaving the economy with weaker growth and firmer inflation at the same time. Summary: The S&P Global flash Australia composite PMI output index fell to 47.7 in October from 51.3, the first contraction in five months and the lowest reading since March. Services activity dropped to 47.8 from 51.9, its first decline since May. The manufacturing PMI edged up to 49.7 from 49.6, and manufacturing output rose to 46.5 from 46.2, still in contraction.

title: HSBC: Gold no short-term hedge for stocks, but three forces keep long-term case intact
body: Spot gold fell to under $4,040 an ounce on Thursday, its lowest since August and roughly a quarter below its January peak. The move came as the Nasdaq dropped more than 2.5%, the kind of joint sell-off HSBC describes. The main pressure on bullion runs through oil: crude (Brent) above $110 a barrel feeds inflation fears, which push up expectations of further Fed tightening and lift Treasury yields and the dollar, raising the cost of holding a metal that pays no interest. Near-term direction is likely to depend on whether equities stabilise and margin pressure eases, and on whether yields pull back from current highs. Steady central bank demand may limit the downside, but it has not been enough to reverse the trend. --- HSBC argues gold still belongs in portfolios for the long run, but warns that when stocks fall, crowded leveraged positions turn the metal into a source of cash rather than protection. Summary: HSBC Asset Management strategists say gold's bull run, which took prices well above $5,000 an ounce earlier this year, has stalled, with prices lower and volatility higher. They say gold has failed to protect portfolios during recent stock market falls, because leveraged positions in gold are sold to meet margin calls. HSBC still sees a strategic case for gold based on the debasement trade, central bank reserve diversification and geopolitical fragmentation. The latest report gives no price target.

The pickup in inflation pushed price growth above the Bank of Japan's 2% target for the first time in nine months, although government fuel subsidies continued to cushion the impact of higher oil prices stemming from the conflict in the Middle East. At the same time, the core index that excludes both fresh food and fuel—closely monitored by the Bank of Japan as a more accurate measure of demand-driven inflation—climbed 2.4% year-on-year in September. That marked its first acceleration since October 2025 and the fastest pace in six months. title: UK Consumer Confidence Sees Biggest Drop Since Pandemic
body: The UK GfK Consumer Confidence Index slumped by 11 points to -24 in October 2026 from -13 in September, its steepest monthly drop since April 2020 and the lowest reading since April.
